binds_to.note: MLM reports consolidated per-ton profitability in its quarterly earnings release, not the 10-K, so the filing panel column is empty. The 10-K gives average selling price by division only (East $21.79, Central $20.13, Southwest $15.70, West $17.22 per ton). Filling this means parsing the release -- deliberately left unchecked rather than proxied from the division figures, which are prices, not unit profits.

Third-party read on industry pricing, independent of company-reported ASP. The thesis is that price per ton compounds; an industry PPI turning negative falsifies that at the sector level, not just for one operator. Divergence between this and company ASP is the tell worth investigating either way.

The counter-cyclical leg. Public infrastructure is what is supposed to cushion a residential downturn; if this turns negative while residential is also falling, the cushion is gone and the cycle claim fails. Federal surface-transportation reauthorisation is the swing factor behind it and has no automated source -- obligations lead outlays lead shipped tons by 2-4 years.

Tracked without a gate, and that is the point. Single-family is the right series (it consumes far more rock per unit than multi-family), and at 808 against a ~1.0M long-run normal it shows real residential stress -- but the thesis explicitly does not depend on residential, so a hard gate here would fire through every housing downturn and train everyone to ignore the ledger. It was gated at first and that was wrong: it painted the whole World Model strip 'broken' on a cyclical reading the thesis already expects. Read it against highway spend -- residential weak AND public weak is the real break.

binds_to.note: The moat, quantified -- and not in XBRL. Disclosed in 10-K Item 2, so it lands via the aggregates reserves filing panel, which is not built yet. Left unchecked rather than estimated. When it does land, the company average is the wrong number to gate on: it hides a depleting quarry inside a critical metro, which is the one that matters. No floor is set until the top-market split exists.
